name: Acapulco Gold
summary: A Mexican sativa associated with the hills around Acapulco in Guerrero, prized for golden-toned flowers and recorded in the US from the mid-1960s. Accounts differ: one book places its roots in neighboring Oaxaca, and some strain guides call it a Mexican x Nepalese cross rather than a pure landrace. One of the three parents of Skunk #1.

evidence.note: Places traditional cultivation in the Guerrero mountains outside Acapulco, citing a 2011 newspaper; notes the first US record in 1964, citing Novak (1979).

disputes.claim: Some strain guides describe it as a native Mexican plant crossed with a Nepalese indica, not a pure landrace

evidence.note: Wikipedia repeats this from strain-guide sites; no primary source is given.
